rules.title: Cartwright Act ban on using or distributing common pricing algorithms as part of an agreement to restrain trade (AB 325)
rules.requirement: Businesses, including landlords and rental software providers, may not use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination, or conspiracy to restrain trade. A common pricing algorithm is any methodology or technology with two or more users that uses competitor data to recommend or influence prices or commercial terms.
rules.key_value: Ban on common pricing algorithms (2+ users, competitor data) used in an agreement to restrain trade
rules.coverage_conditions: Any business in California, including apartment rental companies, that uses, distributes, sells, licenses or provides access to a common pricing algorithm.
rules.exemptions: Single-firm or proprietary algorithms that use only the business's own data are not covered.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where a common pricing algorithm (two or more users, uses competitor data) is used or distributed as part of an agreement to restrain trade.

rules.penalty: Criminal fines up to the greater of $6 million or twice the gain or loss for corporations and $1 million or twice the gain or loss for individuals; civil penalties up to $1 million per violation in AG/district attorney actions (SB 763); treble damages, injunctive relief and attorney's fees in private suits.
rules.quoted_span: Businesses are expressly prohibited from using or distributing common pricing algorithms as part of an agreement to restrain trade.
rules.conflict_note: General antitrust statute, not rental-specific; the source applies it to apartment rental companies by example. Secondary law firm summary; it cites § 16729(a), (b), (d)(3) without stating which subdivision holds which prohibition.

rules.title: Cartwright Act ban on coercing users to adopt common pricing algorithm recommendations (AB 325)
rules.requirement: A business may not use or offer a common pricing algorithm while coercing another person to adopt the algorithm's recommended price or commercial term for the same or similar products or services in California.
rules.coverage_conditions: Users and providers of common pricing algorithms (two or more users, uses competitor data) for products or services in California, including rental housing.
rules.exemptions: Single-firm algorithms using only the business's own data are not covered.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Requires coercion (e.g., imposing negative consequences for not accepting the recommended price or term) involving a common pricing algorithm.

rules.penalty: Criminal fines up to the greater of $6 million or twice the gain or loss for corporations and $1 million or twice the gain or loss for individuals; civil penalties up to $1 million per violation in AG/district attorney actions.
rules.quoted_span: Separately, businesses are also prohibited from using or offering common pricing algorithms if they coerce users to adopt the algorithm s recommendations on pricing or other commercial terms within California for the same or similar products or services.
rules.conflict_note: General antitrust statute, not rental-specific. The source says the meaning of coercion is left open for the courts. Secondary source.
